mainTopic: Which laws of שבת, חגיגה and מעילה are 'like mountains hanging by a hair', and why
overview: The משנה listed areas of law that are 'like mountains hanging by a hair': many laws resting on very little text. The גמרא first explains that הלכות שבת belong on the list because the key rule of מלאכת מחשבת is not written in the שבת section. Next it asks about חגיגות, which seem to be written. רב פפא asks whether 'וחגותם' might only mean 'celebrate', and the גמרא tries to prove from 'חלב חגי' that חג means a קרבן. After a long back-and-forth that proof falls away, and the גמרא learns it instead from a גזירה שוה on the word 'מדבר'. The law still 'hangs by a hair' because that גזירה שוה uses a פסוק from עמוס, and Torah law is not normally learned from נביאים. Then the גמרא turns to מעילה. רמי בר חמא, רבא and רב אשי each offer a different surprising rule as the 'hair', and each answer is challenged in turn. The challenge to רב אשי, based on שמואל, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the laws of שבת hang by a hair
steps.stepSummary: The Torah only forbids planned, purposeful labor on שבת, and that limit is not written in the שבת section itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah forbade only planned, purposeful work, and that idea is not written by שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering an earlier question: why are הלכות שבת called 'hanging by a hair' if they are written in the Torah? The answer is that a basic rule of שבת is not written there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many details of שבת depend on the rule of מלאכת מחשבת, that only planned, purposeful work is forbidden. That rule is not stated in the פסוקים about שבת. So a huge set of laws rests on a source that is not spelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: Planned, purposeful labor: the only kind the Torah forbids on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the pattern for the whole list: a set of laws counts as 'hanging by a hair' when its key foundation is not stated openly in the Torah.

phrases.english: The Torah forbade only planned, purposeful labor,
and 'planned labor' is not written there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this text about הלכות שבת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the key principle has no written source in the שבת section
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The laws of שבת are written in the Torah, so they should not be 'hanging by a hair'
steps.terutzMaskana: The core limit of מלאכת מחשבת is not written by שבת, so these laws do hang by a hair

steps.title: But Festival offerings are written in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, חגיגות, and asks how it can be on the list when it is written in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Festival offerings': but they are written!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה's list, חגיגות, and challenges it. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said חגיגות hang by a hair, meaning they have only a weak source. But the Torah does seem to command a חגיגה offering. So why is it on the list?

keyTerms.meaning: Festival peace offerings brought on the רגלים

phrases.english: 'Festival offerings.'
But they are clearly written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question as was asked about שבת, now aimed at חגיגות
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that חגיגות hang by a hair
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A law that is written in the Torah has a solid source, so it should not be on the list

steps.title: Maybe 'celebrate' does not mean 'bring an offering'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רב פפא's question: who says 'וחגותם' means slaughtering an offering? Maybe it only means 'celebrate'.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed because of what רב פפא said to אביי: how do we know that 'And you shall celebrate it as a festival to ה׳' means slaughtering an offering? Maybe the Torah just means 'celebrate a festival'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word in the Torah is not clearly about an offering. It brings רב פפא's question to show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'וחגותם', which could simply mean 'celebrate'. If so, there is no clear written command to bring a קרבן חגיגה. The doubt itself shows why the law hangs by a hair.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed (for a different point)
And you shall celebrate / bring a חגיגה
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.aramaic: לָא צְרִיכָא, לִכְדַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: No, it is needed because of what Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
From where do we know that this
'And you shall celebrate it as a festival to ה׳'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:41

phrases.english: means slaughtering an offering?
Maybe the Torah is just saying 'celebrate a festival'!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, לִכְדַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 2 by showing the פסוק is not clear
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the written word is unclear, so the law rests on a thin source
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וחגותם' could just mean celebrating, so the offering is not clearly written

steps.title: אביי: then would 'וְיָחוֹגּוּ' also mean just a celebration?
steps.stepSummary: אביי pushes back: if חג just means 'celebrate', then 'that they may celebrate to Me in the wilderness' would also mean just a celebration.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, where it is written 'that they may celebrate to Me in the wilderness', does that also mean just celebrating a festival?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב פפא's idea by testing it on another פסוק with the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the root חג only means 'celebrate', it should mean that in every place. אביי points to משה's request to פרעה, which uses the same word. This sets up his proof in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (then something strange follows)
So too / would it also be the same

phrases.english: But if so, where it is written
'that they may celebrate to Me in the wilderness',
phrases.notes: שמות 5:1

phrases.english: does that also mean just celebrating a festival?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's reading of the word חג
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's idea that חג means only celebrating
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word appears in שמות 5:1, so the reading must also hold there

steps.title: משה asked for sacrifices, so 'חג' means offerings
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves that 'ויחוגו' meant offerings, because משה asked פרעה for sacrifices and burnt offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that is so, isn't it written: 'And משה said: you too must give into our hands sacrifices and burnt offerings'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי blocks the answer 'yes, there too it is only a celebration' by pointing to משה's request for animals to offer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה asked פרעה for זבחים ועולות so they could worship in the desert. That shows the 'celebration' he spoke of meant bringing קרבנות. So the word חג does refer to offerings.

phrases.english: And if you say yes, there too it is just a celebration,
but isn't it written: 'And Moshe said:

phrases.aramaic: גַּם אַתָּה תִּתֵּן בְּיָדֵינוּ זְבָחִים וְעוֹלוֹת״.
phrases.english: you too must give into our hands sacrifices and burnt offerings'?
phrases.notes: שמות 10:25

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's challenge with a proof
steps.raayaObject: That the word חג in 'ויחוגו לי במדבר' refers to offerings
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 10:25, where משה asks for זבחים ועולות

steps.title: Maybe the animals were just for a feast
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe the animals were only for eating and drinking at a celebration, not for offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps this is what the Torah means: 'Eat, drink, and celebrate a festival before Me'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא weakens אביי's proof by suggesting the animals were for a festive meal, not for קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking for animals does not have to mean bringing offerings; the animals could be for a party. If so, חג can still just mean 'celebrate', and רב פפא's doubt comes back.

phrases.english: Perhaps this is what the Torah means:
'Eat, drink, and celebrate a festival before Me'?
phrases.notes: These words are not a פסוק; the גמרא is suggesting what the Torah might mean.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from משה's request
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof that חג means offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Animals could be wanted for a festive meal, so the request does not prove they were קרבנות

steps.title: 'The fat of My festival' seems to prove חג means an offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea: the Torah speaks of 'the fat of My festival', and a plain party has no fat that must be handled before morning, so חג means a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot be, because it is written: 'The fat of My festival shall not remain overnight until morning.' If you think it means just a celebration, does a celebration have fat?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge with a פסוק that ties the word חג to חלב, which only applies to a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls it 'חלב חגי', the fat of My festival, and says it must not be left overnight. That kind of rule only fits an offering, not an ordinary feast. For now this seems to prove that חג means a קרבן, but the next steps attack this proof and the גמרא ends up dropping it.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind; that is impossible
The fat of My festival offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first attempt to find a source for the חגיגה offering. Its weaknesses, shown in the next steps, lead the גמרא to the גזירה שוה of 'מדבר'.

phrases.english: That cannot enter your mind, because it is written:
'The fat of My festival shall not remain overnight until morning',
phrases.notes: שמות 23:18

phrases.english: and if you think it means just a festival celebration,
does a celebration have fat?!
phrases.notes: The point is that a rule about fat fits a קרבן, not an ordinary party.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'just a feast' suggestion and settles the meaning of חג
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק links the word חג to fat, which only applies to an offering
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חג could mean only a festive meal
steps.terutzMaskana: חג in the Torah means a קרבן, as shown by 'חלב חגי'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For now, 'חלב חגי' seems to show that חג means a קרבן. The proof is challenged in the next steps and replaced in step 13.

steps.title: Maybe 'My festival' only means the time the fat is brought
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof from 'חֵלֶב חַגִּי': maybe the verse only means fat brought during festival time, not fat of a special festival קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the Torah means: fat that is brought during the time of a festival may not stay overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 7. Maybe 'חַגִּי' describes when the fat is brought, not a type of קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 the proof worked because 'the fat of My חג' sounded like fat from a festival offering. If 'חג' only names the season, the verse just says that any fat offered during the festival must not stay overnight. Then the verse no longer proves that חג means a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The fats of an animal that are burned on the מזבח
It may not remain overnight (it must not be left until morning)
During the time of a festival
'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah or ה׳

phrases.english: But perhaps this is what the Merciful One is saying:
Fat that is brought at the time of a festival —
"shall not remain overnight"!
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק from שמות 23:18, 'the fat of My festival shall not remain overnight until morning.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof given in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'חֵלֶב חַגִּי' as fat of a festival קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'חַגִּי' could describe the time the fat is offered, so the verse does not prove that חג means a קרבן.

steps.title: Fats may never stay overnight, so festival time cannot be the point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if the verse were about festival time, fats from the rest of the year could stay overnight. But another פסוק shows they may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, only fat brought during a festival may not stay overnight, and fat from the rest of the year may? But it is written 'all night until the morning'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the 'festival time' reading. If that reading were correct, fats brought all year could be left overnight, and that is clearly wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the verse said 'during the festival, fat may not stay overnight', that would suggest that at other times it may. But ויקרא already says fats burn 'all night until the morning', so the rule applies all year. Mentioning the festival time would therefore be pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But now, if so...', which opens an argument that the suggestion leads to a wrong result

phrases.english: But now, if so:

phrases.aramaic: הַבָּא בִּזְמַן חַג — הוּא דְּלֹא יָלִין,
phrases.english: only fat brought at festival time may not remain overnight,
but fat of the whole rest of the year may remain overnight?!
"All night until the morning" is written!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:2. This shows the fats must be finished on the מזבח by morning all year round.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made in Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the suggested reading leads to a false implication
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'חַגִּי' only names the time when the fat is offered.
steps.terutzMaskana: The overnight rule applies all year (ויקרא 6:2), so 'חַגִּי' must refer to a festival קרבן.

steps.title: Maybe the festival verse adds a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ויקרא verse gives only a positive command (עשה), and the festival verse is needed to add a prohibition (לאו).
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps if we had only that verse, I would think it gives a positive command. So this verse is written to give a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 9. Maybe the festival verse is not extra after all, because it adds a לאו to the עשה found in ויקרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said the festival verse would be pointless if it only meant 'festival time'. Now the גמרא says it might have a purpose: ויקרא gives an עשה (burn it all night), and 'לא ילין' adds a לאו. If so, the 'time' reading could stand again.

phrases.english: Perhaps if we learned it from that verse,
phrases.notes: 'That verse' is the one just quoted from ויקרא, 'all night until the morning.'

phrases.english: I would have said:
that one the Merciful One wrote as a positive command,
and this one is for a prohibition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the festival verse would be pointless
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse is not pointless if it turns an עשה into a לאו as well.

steps.title: The prohibition is already written in another verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a לאו against leaving meat overnight is already written in דברים, so the festival verse is not needed for that.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the prohibition, another verse is written: 'And none of the meat that you slaughter in the evening on the first day shall remain until the morning.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects Step 10. The Torah already has a separate verse with a לאו, so 'לא ילין חלב חגי' is not needed to give one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 needed the festival verse to supply a לאו. The גמרא points to דברים 16:4, which already uses the language 'וְלֹא יָלִין' as a prohibition. So the festival verse's purpose still cannot be adding a לאו.

phrases.english: For a prohibition, another verse is written:
"And none of the meat shall remain overnight
phrases.notes: דברים 16:4.

phrases.english: that you slaughter in the evening
on the first day until the morning."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge made in Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to an existing verse that already teaches the point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The festival verse is needed to add a לאו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The לאו is already found in דברים 16:4, so the festival verse is not needed for it.

steps.title: Maybe the verse adds a second prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again: maybe the festival verse is there so that someone who leaves the fat overnight breaks two prohibitions and a positive command.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it comes to make him violate two prohibitions and a positive command!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 11. Even though one לאו already exists, maybe the festival verse adds a second לאו on top of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said the festival verse is not needed for a לאו because דברים already has one. The גמרא answers that the Torah sometimes repeats a prohibition so that the sinner breaks it twice. If so, the festival verse has a purpose, and the 'festival time' reading could come back. The גמרא does not answer this. In the next step it drops the 'חלב חגי' proof and brings a new source.

keyTerms.meaning: To make him violate it, so he is counted as breaking these commands

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say the halacha is two לאוין. It only asks 'maybe', to show the festival verse could still have a purpose.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is to make him violate
two prohibitions and a positive command!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא לַעֲבוֹר עָלָיו בִּשְׁנֵי לָאוִין וַעֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the festival verse is not needed for a לאו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second verse can add another לאו, so the person who leaves the fat overnight breaks two לאוין plus the עשה. That gives the festival verse a purpose.

steps.title: A new source: the word 'wilderness' in two verses
steps.stepSummary: After the 'חֵלֶב חַגִּי' proof is pushed away, the גמרא brings a new proof. It uses a גזירה שוה on the word 'מִדְבָּר' to show that 'וְיָחוֹגּוּ' means bringing animal קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we learn it from the word 'wilderness' appearing in two places. Here it says, 'They shall celebrate for Me in the wilderness.' There it says, 'Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness?' Just as there it means animal sacrifices, so too here it means animal sacrifices.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on the previous proof and brings a brand-new one. It links two פסוקים that both use the word 'מִדְבָּר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in שמות says the people will 'celebrate' (וְיָחוֹגּוּ) in the wilderness, but it does not clearly say they will bring a קרבן. The verse in עמוס uses the same word 'wilderness' and clearly talks about זבחים. Because the same word appears in both, we read the meaning of עמוס into שמות: חגיגה means animal קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It drops the previous idea and starts a new one.
It comes from, meaning it is learned from a link between two פסוקים
It is written here... and it is written there. This is the standard setup for a גזירה שוה.
Just as there... so too here. This carries the meaning from one פסוק over to the other.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source the גמרא settles on for saying that חגיגה means a real קרבן. It sets up the next question about why this source is still called 'hanging by a hair'.

phrases.english: Rather: it is learned from 'wilderness'-'wilderness'.
phrases.notes: The same word appears in two פסוקים, and that link lets us learn one from the other.

phrases.english: It is written here: 'They shall celebrate for Me in the wilderness,'
phrases.notes: שמות 5:1

phrases.english: and it is written there:
'Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness?'
phrases.notes: עמוס 5:25

phrases.english: Just as there it means sacrifices,
so too here it means sacrifices.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 12 left the 'חֵלֶב חַגִּי' proof open to question. This step replaces it with a different source.
steps.raayaObject: That 'וְיָחוֹגּוּ' in שמות means bringing animal קרבנות, not just celebrating
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה on 'מִדְבָּר' between שמות 5:1 and עמוס 5:25

steps.title: So why is it 'hanging by a hair'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if we have a real גזירה שוה, why does the משנה say חגיגה is like mountains hanging by a hair?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does it mean that it is 'like mountains hanging by a hair'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the גמרא has a source, it asks why the משנה still calls this law weakly supported. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's phrase means a lot of law resting on very little text. If a clear גזירה שוה exists, the support seems solid, so the phrase needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: Like mountains hanging by a hair: many laws resting on very thin support from the פסוקים
And what is...? A request to explain

phrases.english: And what is meant by 'like mountains hanging by a hair'?
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's description of the laws of חגיגה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the new source from step 13 fits with the משנה's description
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a law with a גזירה שוה behind it is still called 'hanging by a hair'

steps.title: Because the source is from נביאים, not the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the גזירה שוה uses a פסוק from עמוס, and we do not normally learn תורה laws from נביאים or כתובים. So the support is still thin.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not learn Torah laws from the words of the Prophets and Writings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The proof leans on a פסוק from נביאים, and that is weak support for a תורה law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Half of the גזירה שוה comes from עמוס, which is דברי קבלה. Since תורה law is not normally derived from those books, the law of חגיגה really only hangs on 'a hair'.

keyTerms.meaning: Torah matters: laws from the חמשה חומשי תורה
Words of tradition: the books of נביאים and כתובים

steps.whatToRemember: חגיגה is 'hanging by a hair' because its real source is a גזירה שוה with a פסוק in עמוס, and תורה laws are not normally learned from נביאים.

phrases.english: Torah matters from the words of tradition
phrases.notes: 'Words of tradition' means נביאים and כתובים. עמוס is one of the נביאים.

phrases.english: we do not learn.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִדִּבְרֵי קַבָּלָה לָא יָלְפִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is weak because it depends on a פסוק from נביאים, and תורה law is not normally derived from נביאים or כתובים.

steps.title: But the laws of מעילה are written in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, מעילה. It objects that these laws are clearly written in the תורה, so why call them 'hanging by a hair'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Misuse of holy property: but those laws are written explicitly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic from the משנה, מעילות. Right away it challenges why this belongs on the 'hanging by a hair' list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'hanging by a hair' label fits laws with thin textual support. מעילה has its own clear section in the תורה, so the label seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Misuse of הקדש (holy property) for personal benefit

phrases.english: Misuse of holy property.
But they are clearly written!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:14–16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes with חגיגה and moves to the next item in the משנה's list
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that the laws of מעילה are 'like mountains hanging by a hair'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Laws that are clearly written in the תורה cannot be described as having thin support.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: it refers to the law of the שליח
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא answers that the משנה means one specific rule: if a שליח does what he was sent to do, the בעל הבית is guilty of מעילה. If he did not follow his instructions, the שליח is guilty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: it is needed only for what we learned in a משנה. If an agent did his mission, the owner has committed misuse. If he did not do his mission, the agent has committed misuse.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא explains that 'hanging by a hair' does not mean the basic law of מעילה. It refers to one detail about a שליח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic law is written in the תורה. However, the rule that the בעל הבית is guilty when his שליח follows instructions is not clearly found in the פסוקים, and that rule is the 'hair'.

keyTerms.meaning: For what we learned in a משנה
An agent sent to act for someone else
His mission, the job he was sent to do
The owner, the one who sent the שליח

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said:
It is needed only for what we learned:
phrases.notes: The משנה's words are aimed only at this specific rule, quoted from מסכת מעילה.

phrases.english: An agent who did his mission,
the owner has committed misuse;
if he did not do his mission,
the agent has committed misuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לִכְדִתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing: the phrase applies only to one detail, not to all of מעילה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Hanging by a hair' seemed to describe all the laws of מעילה, which are clearly written.
steps.terutzMaskana: It refers only to the rule that the בעל הבית is liable when his שליח does his mission.

steps.title: Why the שליח rule is surprising
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why this rule is 'hanging by a hair'. It is strange that the שליח does the act but the בעל הבית is the one who is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when he did his mission, why is the owner guilty of misuse? Can one person sin and another become liable? That is what 'like mountains hanging by a hair' means.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the rule from step 17 deserves the label 'hanging by a hair'. This completes רמי בר חמא's answer, which רבא challenges in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the person who does the wrong act is the one held responsible. Here the שליח does the act, but the בעל הבית must bring the קרבן. That goes against our normal sense of fairness, and the פסוקים do not clearly say it.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רמי בר חמא, מעילה as a whole is written in the תורה, and the 'hair' is only the surprising rule that a בעל הבית is liable for what his שליח did on his instructions. רבא rejects this in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: The question 'can one sin and another be liable?' is not a challenge to the rule. The גמרא is pointing out how surprising the rule is, which is exactly why it is called 'hanging by a hair'.

phrases.english: And when he did his mission, why did the owner commit misuse?
Can this one sin and that one become liable?
That is 'like mountains hanging by a hair.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the rule cited in step 17 fits the משנה's description
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The שליח rule in מעילה is unusual, because one person acts and another is liable. Since the פסוקים do not clearly teach it, it is 'like mountains hanging by a hair'.

steps.title: רבא: the agent rule is learned from תרומה, so it is not shaky
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רמי בר חמא. The rule that the owner is liable when his agent does the job is not strange, because מעילה learns agency from תרומה through a גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is so difficult about that? Maybe מעילה is different, because it is learned from תרומה through the word 'sin' that appears in both places. Just as with תרומה a person's agent is like himself, so too with מעילה a person's agent is like himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the answer of רמי בר חמא from Step 17. He says the rule is not 'hanging by a hair' at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא said it is strange that the agent acts but the owner pays. רבא answers that a גזירה שוה from תרומה teaches that an agent counts as the owner himself. So the owner being liable has a solid source, and this cannot be the shaky rule the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: A person's agent is like himself (the basic rule of שליחות)
The portion of produce given to a כהן
'Sin', the shared word that links the two topics

phrases.english: Rava said: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps misuse of consecrated property is different
since it is learned, 'sin' 'sin', from teruma
phrases.notes: The word חטא shows up both in the מעילה section and in the תרומה section, and that shared word links the two.

phrases.aramaic: מָה הָתָם שְׁלוּחוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם כְּמוֹתוֹ
phrases.english: just as there a person's agent is like himself

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן שְׁלוּחוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם כְּמוֹתוֹ?
phrases.english: so too here a person's agent is like himself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רמי בר חמא's explanation from Steps 17-18
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the owner's liability for his agent's act is 'hanging by a hair'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גזירה שוה from תרומה gives a clear source that an agent counts as the owner, so the rule is not thinly supported.

steps.title: רבא's new case: the owner remembers but the agent forgets
steps.stepSummary: רבא offers a different rule as the shaky one. If the owner remembered that the item was הקדש and the agent did not, the agent is liable for מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The משנה is needed only for what a ברייתא teaches. If the owner remembered and the agent did not remember, the agent committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא replaces the answer he just rejected with a new case from a ברייתא. This sets up the next line, which explains why this case is strange.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעילה only applies to someone who acts without knowing. Once the owner remembers that the item is הקדש, he cannot be the one liable, so the liability lands on the agent, who did not know.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
The owner, the one who sent the agent

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said
it is needed only for that which was taught in a baraita
If the owner remembered
phrases.notes: He remembered that the item he sent the agent to use was הקדש.

phrases.english: and the agent did not remember
the agent has committed misuse

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְכִדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new case after rejecting the old one in Step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines which rule the משנה refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The shaky rule is that the owner is liable for his agent's act
steps.terutzMaskana: The shaky rule is that the agent is liable when only the owner remembered

steps.title: Why רבא's case is 'hanging by a hair'
steps.stepSummary: The poor agent only did what he was told, yet he is the one liable. That is why this rule is like mountains hanging by a hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did the poor agent do wrong? This is what the משנה means by 'like mountains hanging by a hair.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what is strange about רבא's case. It ties that case back to the משנה's phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The agent simply followed instructions, and the person who knew the truth was the owner. Making the innocent agent liable seems odd and has little clear source, so it fits the משנה's description.

keyTerms.meaning: Like mountains hanging by a hair: many laws with little clear source

phrases.english: The poor agent, what did he do?
This is 'like mountains suspended by a hair'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the case in Step 20 is 'hanging by a hair'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבא, the shaky rule is that the unknowing agent pays even though he only followed orders.

steps.title: רב אשי: the agent is like anyone who spends הקדש money by mistake
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges רבא. The agent's liability is not strange: he is just like anyone who unknowingly uses הקדש money for ordinary purposes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: What is so difficult? Maybe it is just like the case of someone who spends הקדש money on ordinary things.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects רבא's case from Steps 20-21. He says it is not strange at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the owner remembered, he no longer wanted this job done, so the agent was really acting on his own. An agent acting on his own who unknowingly uses הקדש is liable like anyone else, so nothing here is surprising.

keyTerms.meaning: Money dedicated to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: What is the difficulty?
Perhaps it is just as it is
with one who spends consecrated money for non-sacred purposes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's case from Steps 20-21
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the agent's liability is 'hanging by a hair'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The agent is simply an unknowing user of הקדש, which is the basic case of מעילה, so nothing is strange.

steps.title: רב אשי's new case: the הקדש stone handed to a friend
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings a משנה: someone who picks up a הקדש stone or beam is not liable, but if he hands it to his friend, he is liable and the friend is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: The משנה is needed only for what we learned in a משנה. If someone picked up a stone or beam of הקדש, he has not committed מעילה. If he gave it to his friend, he has committed מעילה and his friend has not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי replaces רבא's case with a different one from a משנה. This sets up the next line, which shows what is strange about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lifting the item alone does not make him liable. Handing it to someone else does make him liable, and the friend who received it is not liable.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said
it is needed only for that which we learned in a mishna

phrases.aramaic: נָטַל אֶבֶן אוֹ קוֹרָה שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ
phrases.english: If one picked up a stone or beam of consecrated property
he has not committed misuse
If he gave it to his friend
he has committed misuse and his friend has not committed misuse

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לִכְדִתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new case after rejecting רבא's case in Step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines which rule the משנה refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The shaky rule is the unknowing agent's liability
steps.terutzMaskana: The shaky rule is that handing a הקדש item to a friend creates liability when picking it up did not

steps.title: Why the stone case is 'hanging by a hair'
steps.stepSummary: He already picked the stone up, so why should it matter whether he keeps it or gives it away? That odd distinction is what 'hanging by a hair' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, he already picked it up. What difference does it make whether he holds it or his friend does? This is what the משנה means by 'like mountains hanging by a hair.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows what is strange about רב אשי's case and ties it to the משנה's phrase. The next step questions this too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picking the item up was the physical act, and the act did not change. Yet handing it over suddenly creates liability. Since that distinction has little obvious basis, it fits 'hanging by a hair.'

keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make to me

steps.whatToRemember: Three attempts to explain the מעילה 'hair': רמי בר חמא says the owner is liable for his agent's act, which רבא rejects. רבא says the agent is liable when only the owner remembered, which רב אשי rejects. רב אשי says handing a הקדש stone to a friend makes him liable, though picking it up did not, and the next step challenges this too.

phrases.english: After all, he already picked it up

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי הוּא וּמָה לִי חֲבֵירוֹ?
phrases.english: what difference is it to me whether he has it or his friend has it?
This is 'like mountains suspended by a hair'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the case in Step 23 is 'hanging by a hair'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רב אשי, the shaky rule is that giving a הקדש item to another person creates liability when lifting it alone did not.

steps.title: What is so difficult about the stone case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רב אשי's example. The stone rule may not be strange at all if we read it the way שמואל does. שמואל's explanation is starting here.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difficulty? Perhaps it is like שמואל's view, for שמואל said: here...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אשי and asks why the stone rule should seem strange. It begins to bring שמואל's explanation, which continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said the stone rule 'hangs by a hair' because picking up the stone already happened, so giving it away should change nothing. The גמרא suggests the rule is not odd at all if the משנה is speaking about a specific case, as שמואל explains. The word הָכָא ('here') signals that שמואל is about to define which case the משנה really means.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difficulty? This asks why something should be seen as a problem at all.
Here, meaning in this case of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to the law of the stone itself. It challenges רב אשי's claim that the law is strange and 'hangs by a hair.'

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty?
phrases.notes: Why call the stone rule strange or 'hanging by a hair' at all?

phrases.english: Perhaps it is like שמואל's explanation,
as שמואל said: here

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's example from steps 23 and 24, which said the stone rule is strange.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that the stone rule (liable only when handing it to a friend) 'hangs by a hair.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה is read as speaking about a specific case, as שמואל explains, the distinction between keeping and handing over makes sense. Then the rule is not strange.
